profile.reading: This building is one of two structures making up SFO4, part of Csquare Silicon Valley campus cluster at 1500 and 1550 Space Park Drive in Santa Clara, California. Csquare, Inc., trading on the New York Stock Exchange as CSQR, is the current name of a data center real estate company whose Silicon Valley facilities trace back to CenturyLink Savvis-heritage colocation assets, divested and rebranded Evoque Data Center Solutions around 2020 to 2021 under Brookfield-affiliated ownership, later Centersquare, and now Csquare ahead of its July 16, 2026 initial public offering. That IPO priced at 21 dollars per share across 50 million shares for roughly 1.05 billion dollars gross, and Brookfield Corporation retained approximately 69 percent of voting power afterward, making Csquare a controlled company under NYSE rules. Per Csquare own SEC registration prospectus, the company overall portfolio as of March 31, 2026 spanned 64 sites across 21 major metro markets in the US, Canada, and the UK, totaling roughly 389 megawatts of sellable power capacity and more than 1,700 customers, with CEO Spencer Mullee and CFO Steven Cook both having joined from the company Evoque-era leadership. That prospectus Properties table lists two Silicon Valley buildings under the SFO4 code, designated SFO4_A at 21,724 rentable square feet, leased, 86.8 percent occupied, and SFO4_B at 35,754 rentable square feet, company-owned and fully occupied at 100 percent, though which specific street address corresponds to which suffix could not be confirmed this session, so no single building-level square footage figure is assigned to this record individually. Whichever unit this record represents, the strong occupancy figures for both SFO4 buildings, especially the fully leased SFO4_B, indicate this is among the more heavily utilized properties in Csquare Silicon Valley portfolio. No tenant is named.

reading.body:
Csquare SFO4 publishes 129.4 MW of combined utility power across 273,000 square feet of technical space in Santa Clara. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 129.4 MW of IT load would support roughly 3,235 racks, but that figure assumes all published utility power reaches IT equipment, which depends on the campus PUE, and the operator does not publish a PUE figure. The actual rack count available for AI workloads is therefore not derivable from the published data.

The certifications describe what the campus is qualified to host. SOC 1 Type 2 and SOC 2 Type 2 qualify it for tenants whose auditors require attested controls over financial and operational systems. PCI DSS qualifies it for payment-card data environments. ISO 27001 and NIST 800-53 qualify it for tenants requiring internationally recognized and US federal information-security management frameworks, respectively. LEED certifies that the building meets a recognized environmental design standard.

In California, this site is one of 103 facilities this site has mapped, and only 8 facilities in the state have a published megawatt figure at all. Among those 8, SFO4 ranks eighth by published MW. The 7 facilities with published figures account for 185 MW combined in this site's dataset, meaning SFO4's 129.4 MW represents roughly 70 percent of that published total on its own, which reflects how few operators in California publish a capacity number rather than indicating SFO4's share of actual statewide capacity.
